mechanism_narrative: The continuing week-over-week rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates a broad return to commuting and foot traffic. That should lift retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks because more weekday trips create more incidental shopping and dining stops.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not average above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise or remain near current levels.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remains depressed, more time at home substitutes for discretionary shopping trips and suppresses retail recreation demand. The effect should appear within two weeks as consumers consolidate errands and reduce nonessential outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points and WORKPLACES stays below -20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 10 and WORKPLACES remaining below -20 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS mobility reflects looser public activity conditions and stronger outdoor circulation, which should spill into higher nearby retail and recreation visits over the following month. The signal is strongest when PARKS and TRANSIT both trend upward together.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks from a level below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days after PARKS crosses upward from below -40 and TRANSIT does not weaken.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while RETAIL_REC remains weak, households are prioritizing necessities over discretionary destinations. That pattern should keep retail and recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks as spending and trips stay concentrated in essential errands.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM moves above 15 and stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT should increase weekday access to retail corridors and recreation venues, translating into a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if only one of the two series improves while the other stays weak.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their current upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in TRANSIT below its recent level signals fewer shared trips and weaker city-center circulation, which should reduce spontaneous retail visits within one week. The effect is immediate because retail outings are often bundled with transit-based commuting.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 and remains there for a week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its prior week after TRANSIT drops below -25 for a full week.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both stay high while GROCERY_PHARM rises, the mobility mix implies localized activity and fewer discretionary cross-town trips. That combination should depress retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks because leisure and shopping are displaced by home-centered routines.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays below -30 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 10.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent narrowing of the gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL indicates a gradual normalization of out-of-home activity. If that convergence continues for four weeks, retail and recreation mobility should move higher because more people are spending time away from home and combining trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last 28-day mean over the next 28 days even as WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls or flattens.
